paragraphs: A scroll-driven 3D experience that renders real-time shadow mapping with Three.js.

Shadow Map is an interactive technical demo that visualises how directional light shadows work in real-time 3D rendering. It combines a custom Three.js scene with a scroll-driven narrative powered by GSAP, guiding the viewer through the core concepts of shadow mapping — from the directional light source to the PCF filtering that produces soft edges.

The experience begins with a wide, atmospheric landscape. As the user scrolls, the camera lifts to reveal a monumental "THREE.JS" inscription, then transitions into an overlay that explains each component of the shadow pipeline through horizontally scrolling cards.
features: Real-time shadows — Directional light casting shadows at 4096×4096 resolution with PCF (Percentage-Closer Filtering) for soft edges.
Scroll-driven narrative — A cinematic camera move followed by a fade transition into an educational overlay, all synchronised with the user's scroll via GSAP ScrollTrigger.
Animated wildlife — Six horses, a flamingo, a stork, and a parrot roam the scene, each with looped morph animations that play asynchronously.
3D typography — A bold, beveled "THREE.JS" text geometry sits embedded in the terrain, acting as the visual anchor of the scene.
Shadow map HUD — Press T to toggle an inset view of the shadow map texture, revealing exactly what the light sees.
